transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. Um, I came in because... well, I work in retail, and lately I just can't make myself go near the front windows of the store, or even that part of the street anymore. I keep finding excuses to just stay in the back room, even though being out on the floor is a big part of my job. It's just getting really hard to deal with.
Can you tell me more about why you avoid the front windows and that part of the street? Is it more about feeling unsafe in public places, or are you worried about being watched or judged by others?

Um, it's not really about being judged or watched by people. And I don't think it's about public places in general, either, because I can go to the grocery store or the mall on my days off just fine. 

It's really just... that specific part of the street and the windows facing it. Whenever I have to go up to the front of the store, I just get this really overwhelming, awful feeling. I'm not entirely sure how to explain it, to be honest. It's just that exact spot that makes me feel really tense, so I just stay away from it.

When you're near that part of the store or the front windows, do you experience sudden physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, trembling, or shortness of breath, or is it more of a general feeling of dread or tension?

Um, I don't really get those sudden physical things you mentioned, like the racing heart or sweating. It's not like a panic attack or anything like that. 

It's definitely more of just... a really strong feeling of dread and tension. Like this heavy, awful feeling in my chest that just makes me want to get away from there as fast as I can. But I haven't noticed my heart pounding or feeling out of breath or anything. Just that really bad feeling of dread.
Has something happened to you in that specific area near the front windows or on that part of the street that makes you feel this way, or does it seem to come out of nowhere?

No, it definitely didn't come out of nowhere. Um, something did happen. This has all been going on for about two weeks now... ever since a car crashed right through the store window while I was working an overnight shift. So, yeah, since that night, I just can't bring myself to be in that spot.
Since the accident, do you feel like your reaction to being near that area is more intense or longer-lasting than you would expect given the actual danger now?

Um, I don't really know if I'd say that. I haven't really thought about what I'd expect, to be honest. 

I mean, the window is boarded up now, so I guess there isn't any actual danger of it happening again today... but it doesn't feel like I'm overreacting, if that makes sense. A car did just crash right into the building where I work. So, I'm not really sure if the feeling is more intense than it should be. I just know I really, really don't want to go near that spot.
Since the accident, have you had any moments where you feel like you're re-living the crash, like seeing images of it in your mind or feeling the same fear you felt that night?

Yeah, I do. The crash just... keeps popping into my head out of nowhere. It happens a lot when I'm trying to set up displays at work. It's like, suddenly I can hear that huge bang again, and I just see the glass coming down. It really feels like it's happening all over again right in that moment.
